text:
Michael: heads-up — after yesterday's pretokenizer rewrite we’re seeing host-side tail latency regressions on streaming requests, p99 up ~18%.
Sara: saw that on the dashboards, looks correlated with grpc small-write paths and HPACK encode time.
Jamal: i captured a perf trace — allocator churn in parse stage and extra memcpy when we splice frames. attaching snippet: `trace://link/abc123`
Izzy: odd, the change was meant to move tokenization earlier to enable KV caching. did we accidentally introduce double-copy on the stream path?
Michael: yes, patch added a PreTokenize->Serialize step that copies proto into a temp buffer before handing to grpc. p50 cost unchanged, but p95/p99 show spikes at the proto serialize boundary.
Sara: raw numbers from today's canary: host-parse median 1.1ms, p95 8.2ms, p99 24.7ms. previous p99 was ~21ms. CPU samples show `memcpy` and `proto::Serialize` hotspots.
Jamal: hypothesis: we lost zero-copy path for small chunk frames due to the splice logic change. Also HPACK compression CPU went up when frames are aligned differently.
Izzy: quick experiment idea — detect small frames (<1KB) and use writev to emit header+payload without intermediate buffer. fallback to current path for larger frames.
Michael: can we try a patch that uses `IOVec` for smallframes + reuse preallocated slab? low-risk revert-ish.
Sara: also KV cache warmup: because we pretokenize earlier, we insert into KV with slightly different key shape which reduces hit-rate for short-lived requests. p10 hit-rate dropped 2pt. we should normalize key material.
Jamal: agreed. I can roll a tiny change that canonicalizes prefix keys before caching. test locally shows +1.8pt hit-rate.
Izzy: for the writev patch I sketched this quick change:
```
if (frame.size() < 1024) {
  iovec[0] = header;
  iovec[1] = frame.payload;
  ::writev(fd, iovec, 2);
} else {
  current_write(frame);
}
```
Should avoid extra allocs.
Michael: nice. add a metrics tag for writev_path=true and measure.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started for `pretokenizer-rewrite` at 2024-05-12T09:12:00Z :rocket:
Sara: also add a perf test in qemu unit that simulates 2000 concurrent streaming short messages to catch regressions in CI.
Jamal: i'll own the writev canary and the KV canonicalization. Izzy, can you add the perf-ci scenario?
Izzy: yes, will add scenario + baseline script. plan: canary + collect p50/p95/p99, KV hit-rate and writev success ratio.
Michael: timeline — merge small fixes today, canary 2 hours, roll back if p99 still > baseline +10%.
Sara: FYI I'll update the rollout doc and add rollback runbook snippet for this class of host-side alloc regressions.
Michael: thanks team. keep updates in thread.
Sara: noted :thumbsup:
